newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq, SEC agree to delay new order rules.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq, SEC agree to delay new order rules.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission and Nasdaq have agreed to delay implementation of new limit-order rules to January 20 from January 13, Nasdaq said Wednesday.
The later start date "will give all market participants additional time for testing," National Association of Securities Dealers (NASD) Executive Vice President Richard Ketchum said in a statement.
"Our testing has gone very well, and we think our systems are ready," he said, adding that he was pleased by the SEC decision to delay, calling it a "a prudent move."

The SEC-approved limit-order rule, which covers trading orders ranging in size from 100 to 10,000 shares, will benefit retail customers and institutions that put together orders on behalf of small investors.
Limit orders -- those in which customers specify the price at which they wish to trade -- will initially be displayed for 50 of the most actively traded stock on Nasdaq.
The rules also apply to other exchanges, such as the New York Stock Exchange, but for the most part those markets are already in compliance.
NASD is the parent of Nasdaq.
